name: WhiteFiber

logo.source: whitefiber.com home page header logo (inline SVG, viewBox 154x20); no Wikipedia page exists. The site draws the mark with currentColor (white on its dark header), so it is saved here with the fill set to black

description: WhiteFiber does two things with AI computing. It rents GPU capacity by the month to AI developers (cloud services, 80 percent of H1 2026 revenue), and it builds small, high-density data centers and leases the power and space to tenants who bring their own hardware (colocation, 19 percent). The two pay very differently: cloud contracts are short and lumpy, so its first customer, a single GPU buyer that was 71 percent of 2025 revenue, terminated in Q2 2026 and paid a $12.3M termination fee that propped up the quarter, while colocation contracts are long and fixed, with $933M of the $1.0B contracted backlog, led by Nscale (about $865M over ten years at the North Carolina NC-1 site) and Cerebras (five years at Montreal MTL-3). It is majority-owned (about 70 percent) by Bit Digital and is still loss-making: a $15.0M net loss in Q2 2026 on $28.8M of revenue, with $310M of convertible notes raised in August 2026 to fund the data center build. Colocation tenants, not cloud customers, are what the backlog depends on, so delivery of NC-1 to Nscale (now expected from Q3 2026) is the main execution risk.

hq.note: 31 Hudson Yards, Floor 11, Suite 30, New York, NY 10001 (8-K cover, 2026-08-18). Data centers are in Montreal and Saint-Jerome (Quebec) and Madison NC; cloud GPUs are also hosted in Iceland and Atlanta.

businessLines.name: Cloud Services (GPU cloud)
businessLines.how: Customers sign service orders for a set number of GPUs for a set term, from two weeks to five years, and pay monthly; pricing depends on GPU type, quantity and duration, and some contracts are usage-based or month-to-month after the initial term. WhiteFiber owns or leases the GPU servers (large GPU lease expense from sale-leasebacks) and rents the hosting space, so margin is revenue less lease, power and support costs.
businessLines.description: Dedicated GPU capacity (H100, H200, B200, GB200, B300 and, from 2027, Vera Rubin) for AI training and inference, sold to AI developers and other AI cloud companies. GPUs sit in third-party data centers in Iceland (Blanda campus, 6 MW gross), Atlanta, and (from Q4 2026) Sydney and France, plus WhiteFiber's own Montreal sites. First GB200 NVL72 shipment arrived April 2025.

revenue.note: FY2025 $68.754M; FY2024 $45.728M; Q2 2026 $23.806M vs $16.595M. Q2 2026 includes a $12.3M termination fee from the Initial Customer.

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2025 $68.754M; FY2024 $45.728M; Q2 2026 $23.806M vs $16.595M. Q2 2026 includes a $12.3M termination fee from the Initial Customer.

operatingProfit.note: FY2025 segment gross profit $42.167M, margin 61.3%, 88.5% of the two segments' total. Share is of total segment gross profit $29.632M. No segment operating profit after depreciation or G&A is reported.

businessLines.name: Colocation Services (data centers)
businessLines.how: Multi-year leases (five to ten years) at a fixed monthly fee based on committed power in kilowatts or megawatts, with annual escalators and pass-through of electricity and some operating costs to the tenant; customers install and run their own servers. Revenue starts only when a facility is built, energized and accepted.
businessLines.description: Tier-3 data center space, power and cooling leased to customers who run their own AI hardware: MTL-1 (4 MW gross, Montreal, fully leased), MTL-2 (5 MW gross, under redevelopment, delivery near end of 2026), MTL-3 (Saint-Jerome, 7 MW gross, operational November 2025, Cerebras 5 MW IT load), NC-1 (Madison, North Carolina, Nscale 40 MW phase, billing not yet started). Company target 76 MW gross by end of Q4 2026 and a pipeline of about 1,500 MW under review at 2025-12-31. A further North Carolina property (Yadkin County) for $60.0M cash was agreed 2026-08-16.

revenue.note: FY2025 $8.914M; FY2024 $1.361M; Q2 2026 $4.726M vs $1.729M. Segment revenue including a small intersegment amount was $9.535M in H1 2026.

operatingProfit.note: FY2025 segment gross profit $5.463M, margin 61.3%, 11.5% of the two segments' total.

businessLines.name: Equipment leasing (other revenue)
businessLines.how: Lease payments on equipment leased to customers; small and not expected to grow.
businessLines.description: Data storage and network equipment leased to customers under sales-type leases.

whatsNext.text: Delivery of the first 40 MW phase at NC-1 to Nscale expected in Q3 2026, with revenue starting 30 days after completion (previously expected from June 2026)
Paris-region five-year AI compute contract (over $160M) expected to start in September 2026; project financing term sheet signed but definitive documents not finalized at the 10-Q date
Baseten Labs 1,392 B300 GPUs begin revenue in November 2026; Iceland 576 B300 GPUs (about $87.5M, five years) targeted for December 2026
MTL-2 construction starts in Q3 2026 with delivery near the end of the fiscal year; company target of 76 MW gross total data center capacity by the end of Q4 2026
Sydney 2.5 MW cloud capacity lease starts in Q4 2026; Prime Intellect Vera Rubin deployment (576 GPUs, about $108.2M) targeted for Q2 2027
Commercial launch of a cross-data-center networking product targeted for Q3 2026, subject to further testing
